headline: Siri AI app on iOS 27 lets users easily switch between Siri and ChatGPT
summary: The new Siri AI app on iOS 27 defaults to Siri, but provides a quick way to switch to ChatGPT at any time. This integration offers users more flexibility in their AI assistant choice.
details: The new Siri AI app in iOS 27 introduces a key feature allowing users to seamlessly switch between Apple's native Siri and OpenAI's ChatGPT. While Siri remains the default assistant, a quick toggle enables access to ChatGPT for more advanced conversational AI capabilities.

This functionality is part of the iOS 27 beta 2 release. Additionally, Apple has instructed Siri AI to explicitly decline requests to summarize URLs, indicating specific boundaries for its integrated AI features.
caption:
iOS 27's new Siri AI app allows seamless switching between Siri and ChatGPT. Get the best of both AI worlds directly from your iPhone.

The new Siri AI app in iOS 27 introduces a key feature allowing users to seamlessly switch between Apple's native Siri and OpenAI's ChatGPT. While Siri remains the default assistant, a quick toggle enables access to ChatGPT for more advanced conversational AI capabilities.

This functionality is part of the iOS 27 beta 2 release. Additionally, Apple has instructed Siri AI to explicitly decline requests to summarize URLs, indicating specific boundaries for its integrated AI features.

headline_marked: GitHub ships a [[one-click self-revoke]] for users whose credentials just leaked
headline: GitHub ships a one-click self-revoke for users whose credentials just leaked
summary: GitHub's new self-service credential revocation flow allows users to revoke all personal access tokens, SSH keys, OAuth tokens, and SSO authorizations in a single action, drastically cutting down incident response time.
details: GitHub has introduced a new one-click self-service credential revocation flow, announced on June 24. This feature allows users to instantly revoke or delete all personal access tokens, SSH keys, OAuth tokens, and SSO authorizations from a single view under Settings, Credentials.

Previously, containing a credential leak involved a manual scavenger hunt across multiple separate menus for different credential types. This often led to crucial credentials being missed during a high-stress incident.

The new consolidated view significantly reduces containment time from hours to minutes, a critical factor in mitigating damage from token replay attacks against build platforms, registries, and deploy keys. Every minute saved directly limits attacker access.

While powerful, this 'revoke-everything' action is destructive by design, signing users out of all integrations. Recovery is a separate process, requiring careful re-authorization of necessary services and applications.

This move complements existing enterprise-owner bulk revocation capabilities and acknowledges that 'rotate everything' is a real user action performed under stress. GitHub is moving beyond treating token hygiene as mere documentation, providing a concrete tool for incident response.
caption:
Leaked credentials? GitHub now offers a single button to revoke all personal access tokens, SSH keys, and OAuth authorizations instantly.

GitHub has introduced a new one-click self-service credential revocation flow, announced on June 24. This feature allows users to instantly revoke or delete all personal access tokens, SSH keys, OAuth tokens, and SSO authorizations from a single view under Settings, Credentials.

Previously, containing a credential leak involved a manual scavenger hunt across multiple separate menus for different credential types. This often led to crucial credentials being missed during a high-stress incident.

The new consolidated view significantly reduces containment time from hours to minutes, a critical factor in mitigating damage from token replay attacks against build platforms, registries, and deploy keys. Every minute saved directly limits attacker access.

While powerful, this 'revoke-everything' action is destructive by design, signing users out of all integrations. Recovery is a separate process, requiring careful re-authorization of necessary services and applications.

This move complements existing enterprise-owner bulk revocation capabilities and acknowledges that 'rotate everything' is a real user action performed under stress. GitHub is moving beyond treating token hygiene as mere documentation, providing a concrete tool for incident response.
